spec.definition: Caffeine half-life is the amount of time it takes for the concentration of caffeine in the blood to reduce to half of its initial value.

prediction.prompt: Caffeine's half-life is about 5 hours. You drink a coffee at 9 a.m. What percent of that caffeine is still in your body at midnight, 15 hours later?

extremes.watch: Very fast metabolism clears almost all caffeine in 10 hours.
Slow metabolism means 50% is still present after 10 hours.

misconceptions.label: Two half-lives and it's gone
misconceptions.why_tempting: Half gone in 5 hours sounds like all gone in 10.
misconceptions.refutation: Each 5 hours removes half of what's left: 100 to 50 to 25 to 12.5 percent.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified

misconceptions.label: It only halves once
misconceptions.why_tempting: The half-life sounds like a one-time drop, then it levels off.
misconceptions.refutation: The halving repeats every half-life, so the amount keeps shrinking.
misconceptions.source_note: Page states the correct model; that this mistake is common is unverified
